ai.title: codebuff 1.0.439
ai.summary: Package version bumped to 1.0.439 in npm-app/release/package.json. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant's coding helper, you're now on a newer snapshot (released starting 2025-07-24) that includes mostly small refinements rather than a big visible change. You'd notice a couple of things while working: when you paste in a half-finished piece of JSON, the assistant is less likely to mangle it by carelessly adding a closing brace at the end of a number, and a couple of behind-the-scenes behaviors around how the assistant stops and reports what it's doing have been tidied up. The headline number you see in your tool (1.0.439) is just a label this time; the actual work is the batch of minor fixes that shipped alongside it.

ai.title: Add nightly evals workflow and increase eval concurrency
ai.summary: New `.github/workflows/nightly-evals.yml` runs `bun run-eval-set` daily at 9:00 AM UTC via cron, using Bun 1.2.12 and a 360-minute timeout. Existing `.github/workflows/evals.yml` concurrency raised from 1 to 10. Both workflows share the same eval execution command with email notifications enabled.

eli5.text: Starting today, the team added a new automated check that runs the assistant's quality tests every night at 9 AM UTC, so problems are caught even when no one is actively watching. They also sped up the existing daily check to test ten things at once instead of one, which means results come back faster during the day. You wouldn't see anything new on your screen, but behind the scenes the system is keeping a closer eye on how the assistant behaves and catching issues sooner.

ai.title: Strip /$bunfs binary path from CLI args
ai.summary: npm-app/src/index.ts filters leading /$bunfs path injected by Bun before constructing initialInput. Fixes command-line argument parsing when launching compiled binary. Scope: npm-app CLI entrypoint.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant from the command line with an extra instruction, a stray piece of internal path text used to sneak in at the very beginning, messing up how that instruction was interpreted. The program now quietly removes that stray bit before reading your instruction, so what you typed is understood exactly as intended. If you launch the assistant this way, you won't notice anything different except that your starting message now reads cleanly instead of beginning with cryptic path characters.

ai.title: Shorten tool parameter names in common constants
ai.summary: Renamed tool parameter identifiers from codebuff_tool_name and codebuff_easp to cb_tool_name and cb_easp in common/src/constants/tools.ts. This change reduces token usage for tool definitions. Scope is limited to shared core constants. No migration logic is included; consumers must use the new names.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal tool tags now use shorter labels (cb_tool_name and cb_easp instead of codebuff_tool_name and codebuff_easp) when it calls tools, which slightly reduces the amount of text sent during conversations. This is a behind-the-scenes change that does not alter any visible behavior, so you should not notice any difference whether you are chatting, running commands, or watching the assistant work.

ai.title: Add git commit message example to run-terminal-command
ai.summary: Added a `git commit` example to the `run-terminal-command` tool definition showing heredoc usage for multi-line messages with Co-Authored-By. Reordered imports in `prompts.ts` and normalized a curly apostrophe. Internal change affecting backend tool definitions and system prompts.

eli5.text: When the assistant creates a Git commit, it now offers a ready-made example showing exactly how to write a multi-line commit message in the terminal, including the standard closing credit line for Codebuff. You would see a new sample command appear inside the run-terminal-command tool definition, alongside the reordered import statements and a small cleanup of a curly apostrophe that together make the underlying instruction file tidier. This is live today in the internal tool definitions and system prompts, so any assistant that already relies on those prompts gets the updated guidance.

ai.title: Add chunk logging to agent stream parser
ai.summary: Agent step processing now logs individual stream chunks alongside the full response. `processStreamWithTools` in `backend/src/tools/stream-parser.ts` accumulates chunks in a `fullResponseChunks` array, returning it alongside the joined `fullResponse` string. This change propagates to `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`, where `fullResponseChunks` is passed to downstream logging and state updates. The `xml-stream-parser.ts` refactor simplifies `lastIndex` initialization in `extractToolCalls`.

eli5.text: The system that runs the agent step now records each individual piece of the streamed reply, not just the final assembled reply. If you watched the logs for an agent step, you would see the same pieces that made up the total response logged on their own, alongside the joined full response, so debugging a step shows every chunk that arrived. The change is internal, so it does not add a visible feature for readers, but it does make the logging of how a reply was built more detailed than before.

ai.title: Update tool call schema in tests
ai.summary: Renamed codebuff_tool_name to cb_tool_name in test fixtures and XML stream parser tests. Removed codebuff_end_step field from add_subgoal example. Aligns test data with current tool call schema.

eli5.text: The internal test system that verifies how the assistant reads and reacts to tool instructions was updated to match the current naming and structure of those instructions. The example data files used by the tests now use the shortened name for the tool and drop a status field that is no longer tracked. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping that keeps the test suite in sync with the live system; it does not change anything you can see or do.

ai.title: codebuff 1.0.440
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.440 in npm-app/release/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you opened the assistant today, you would see it reports version 1.0.440 instead of 1.0.439, but nothing else would look different because the change is just a version label with no new features. Behind the scenes, this update also adds a nightly testing routine that runs more evaluations at once, so the assistant is now being checked more thoroughly each day. It also cleans up its command-line input handling, renames a few internal tool settings for clarity, includes an example of how to write a multi-line Git commit, and logs extra details while processing responses. None of these are visible to you while using the assistant, but they help keep it stable and well-tested.

ai.title: Add -p print mode to release/index.js
ai.summary: Added `-p` flag to `npm-app/release/index.js` via `commander`. Suppresses terminal UI updates and switches error/info logs to JSON format when active. Scope limited to release script and its `package.json` dependencies.

eli5.text: If you run the release tool with a new print flag, it stops showing the live terminal progress display and instead outputs information as structured JSON that other programs can read. This only affects the release script that publishes the software, so most people will notice no difference unless they are running that specific release process. The tool now quietly does this when the flag is given, otherwise it behaves exactly as before.

ai.title: Support handleSteps generator functions in dynamic agent templates
ai.summary: Dynamic agent templates now support `handleSteps` generator functions for programmatic control. `load-agents.ts` converts these functions to strings during loading, while `dynamic-agent-service.ts` validates their presence and format. The `DynamicAgentConfigSchema` in `common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts` accepts the optional generator, and `dynamic-agents.knowledge.md` documents the new TypeScript-based discovery process.

eli5.text: You can now write custom AI assistants using a special scripting style that lets you define exactly how each step of the assistant should run, giving you precise control over things like which tools it uses and in what order. When you place one of these script files in your agents folder, the system checks that the script follows the correct format before activating the agent, and if the script is missing or formatted wrong, the agent will be skipped with a clear explanation. A sample script showing how to use this feature is included so you can copy and adapt it for your own assistants.

ai.title: init-worktree script handles existing branches
ai.summary: scripts/init-worktree.ts now creates worktrees from existing branches instead of failing. If git branch exists, script logs warning and uses `git worktree add <path> <branch>`; otherwise uses `-b` flag. Affects internal dev tooling only. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: When developers ask the project to set up a separate workspace (a 'worktree'), the helper tool no longer crashes if a branch with that name already exists. Instead of erroring out, it now quietly notices the branch is there and creates the workspace pointing at the existing branch rather than trying to make a new one. Only internal development tooling behaves this way; there is nothing a regular user would see or change about how the software works.
